provenance: curated in-repo benchmark corpus, authored as labelled fixture pairs. This is SELF-CURATED ground truth (the tests were written from the rule contracts, including reported-defect fixtures reproduced in the v1.5.2 fix commit and, for the v1.5.3 additions, fixtures reproduced against the unmodified 874bec1 tree through the real scanner path before fixing). It is NOT a general-purpose recall claim; see BENCHMARKS.md and METHODOLOGY.md for scope statements.
matching_rules: A vulnerable case is a TP when exactly one finding has rule==expected.rule on the manifest file (extension-stripped; route files are matched by their full relative path) and an exact absolute line match, with severity at or above severity_floor.

Multiple findings for one underlying defect collapse to the primary expected rule; secondary findings (advisory notes such as RES-003, or additional true rules on the same vulnerable file, e.g. AUTHZ-001 next to TEN-002) are neither TP/FN nor FP and are excluded from precision arithmetic.

Safe cases expect ZERO findings above LOW severity; a finding above LOW on a safe file counts as a false positive. LOW-severity review notes are advisory (no score) and are only tolerated on a safe case when the manifest lists them under allowed — otherwise they count as FP.
Line numbers are exact-absolute by contract (deterministic scanner); a finding on the wrong line counts as FN, not TP.

Destructured request.json() field fetched directly.

service_role JWT hardcoded in a 'use client' component (honeypot seed lineage).

Reported defect fixture (v1.5.3): a 'use client' component imports the secret module through the CONFIGURED `@vuln/*` path alias (tsconfig paths at the scan root) — client-reachable CRITICAL, previously reported only as the unclassified-medium review.
Same mutating write as the vulnerable pair but with a recognizable authz call — the missing-evidence rule must stay silent.
Non-authorization body fields (displayName/eventId) with an in-handler authz gate — AUTHZ-002 must not fire on ordinary fields.
The decision reads a DATABASE record (u.role), not request data — must stay silent.
Hard-coded fetch destination — no tainted sink argument.

Recognized host-allowlist validation demotes the finding to the LOW no-score review note — adjudicated as correct calibration (the scanner never claims a URL safe that it cannot verify), NOT a false positive.
Same destructive read with an organizationId predicate and an authz gate.

Committed .env with placeholder '<...>' values only — secret rules must stay silent; the tracked-.env hygiene rule emits exactly its documented LOW no-score review note (public values only), adjudicated as correct calibration.
anon key accessed via process.env server-side — the documented-correct pattern.

Reported-defect counterpart (v1.5.3): a Stripe webhook that DOES verify the signature (constructEvent call shape) must not be reported as unauthenticated (NEXT-004/AUTHZ-001 silent — the FP reproduced on this shape before the fix).

Server-only module (env-based key) imported through the SAME configured `@safe/*` path alias mechanism as the vulnerable counterpart — env access in a server module is the documented-correct pattern; no leak claim without a client-reachable secret value.

`export { handler as DELETE }` where handler is an IMPORT (no local function-shaped declaration) — no handler is fabricated, so no missing-authz review fires (arbitrary export aliases are not handler evidence).

`Set.has(new URL(t).hostname)` — Set membership over the URL hostname IS a destination-validation operation → demotes to the LOW no-score review note (same adjudication as the includes-based allowlist case).
